checks.label: Find the cosine as the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse, and the sine as the opposite side over the hypotenuse: on the first screen, at every angle φ from 0° to 90°, the 10 A arrow's floor shadow is drawn 10 × cos φ and its wall shadow 10 × sin φ, and at 60° the rows give 10 cos 60° = 5 A and 10 sin 60° = 8.66 A

Because true power and apparent power form the adjacent and hypotenuse sides of a right triangle, the power factor ratio is also equal to the cosine of that phase angle: at every φ the power triangle has a right angle where its flat and upright sides meet, flat ÷ long side = cos φ, and at 60° the rows give 1150 ÷ 2300 = 0.5 = cos 60°

With the current held at 10 A, dragging the current arrow further behind keeps the long side at 2300 VA while the flat side, the true power, shrinks as 2300 × cos φ at every degree: its label reads 2300 W at 0°, 1150 W at 60° and 0 W at 90°

Power Factor is the cosine of the angle between the Real Power and the Apparent Power, pf = kW/kVA = cos(φ): with Hold true power on, at every φ up to 72.5° the drawn flat side stays 10 kW, the long side is 10 ÷ cos φ kVA at the angle φ to it, so kW ÷ kVA = cos φ

If the power factor of the load is 0.6 (cos 53°), the total current in the line will be 72.5 A, and correcting the PF to 0.8 (cos 37°) would reduce the current to 54.5 A: holding 10 kW on 230 V, the current bar is drawn 72.5 A long at 0.6 and 54.3 A at 0.8, within 0.2 A of the printed 54.5 A

With Hold true power on, φ stops at a power factor of 0.3 (72.5°), where the current is 145 A; up to there the current rises at every step up in φ, and the plot traces it from a power factor of 1 down to the setting

The mains voltage in the UK can vary between 216 and 253 volts, and these are r.m.s. values: the power wave multiplies a voltage wave peaking at 230 × √2 by a current wave peaking at 10 × √2, so at every φ its average over whole cycles is 230 × 10 × cos φ, the flat side; at 0° it never dips below the line and touches it twice a cycle, and at 90° its humps above and below are equal
The voltage declared in respect of a low voltage supply shall be 230 volts between the phase and neutral conductors: the voltage arrow is labelled 230 V, and the working multiplies by 230
60 Hz is the most common frequency adopted for use on board ship: the mixed puzzle on a ship's supply works from 60 turns a second, and its answer is 2π × 60 = 377 radians a second

The motor's triangle is drawn 621 VA long and 450 W flat at 43.6°, its upright side √(621² − 450²) = 428 VAr; the slip triangle, with power factor taken as sin φ, is drawn at 46.4° with a flat side of only 428 W

Each puzzle accepts only its right answer, and each mixed puzzle first only its right tool; every wrong answer and wrong tool has its own hint, every wrong answer its own red row of working, the answer appears once given, and before it nothing in the picture gives it away

On the two-currents puzzle both branch arrows keep their labels at every stage: before a tool is picked, with each tool picked, once the arrows lie tip to tail, and once answered right, wrong or with Why? open

No label sits on another label or a handle, or runs off the picture, on any screen in any state: puzzles answered right, wrong or with Why? open, every tool picked, φ dragged from 0° to 90°, with Hold true power on and off
Every demonstration has finished within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; each answer, tool and Why? has settled within 1.8 s
